name: Afghanistan
summary: A mountainous state founded as the Durrani Empire by Ahmad Shah Durrani in 1747. It was a buffer between the Russian and British empires, then went through monarchy, Soviet war, civil war and Taliban rule.

knownFor.label: Afghan carpets
knownFor.note: Hand-knotted wool carpets, often deep red.

knownFor.label: Buzkashi
knownFor.note: A horseback game where riders fight for a goat carcass.

knownFor.label: Ahmad Shah Durrani
knownFor.note: Founder of the Durrani Empire, seen as the father of Afghanistan.

location.value: Landlocked, at the crossroads of Central and South Asia; about 653,000 km².

terrain.value: Mostly mountainous, with plains in the north and south-west separated by the Hindu Kush.

climate.value: Continental: harsh winters in the central highlands and north-east, hot summers in the low-lying south-west.

resources.value: Lithium, iron, zinc, copper and other minerals; lapis lazuli mined in Badakhshan since ancient times.

disasters.value: Earthquakes, such as the Herat earthquake of October 2023, which killed over 1,400 people; severe droughts.

urbanisation.value: Kabul is the capital and largest city; the Ring Road links it with Kandahar, Herat and Mazar-i-Sharif.

disease.value: Healthcare has improved since 2000, but life expectancy is the lowest of any country outside Africa.

migration.value: The Soviet–Afghan War displaced about 6 million people, mainly to Pakistan and Iran.

economicBase.value: Services and agriculture; opium was the major crop until Taliban campaigns cut poppy growing by over 80% in the south (2023).

tradeRoutes.value: Silk Road routes once linked it to China, India, Persia and Central Asia.

wealth.value: One of the world’s least developed countries, despite large mineral deposits.

inequality.value: Large gaps between cities and the countryside, and between men and women.

governmentType.value: Durrani monarchy from 1747; republic after 1973; communist rule from 1978; Taliban Islamic Emirate (1996–2001, and again since 2021).

keyRulers.value: Ahmad Shah Durrani. Dost Mohammad Khan. Amanullah Khan. Zahir Shah. Hamid Karzai.

succession.value: Royal succession, then coups, elections (2004–2019) and Taliban rule.

institutions.value: The loya jirga (grand assembly), held since at least 1747, most recently in 2022.

stability.value: Unstable since the 1973 coup: a communist coup (1978), the Soviet invasion (1979–89), civil wars, and war after the 2001 US invasion until 2021.

eliteConflict.value: Rivalries between ethnic and political factions.

majorWars.value: Anglo-Afghan Wars (the third in 1919); Soviet–Afghan War (1979–89); the 2001 US-led invasion and war until 2021.

territoryChange.value: The Durand Line (1893) set the border with British India; it remains a source of tension with Pakistan.

alliancesRivals.value: A buffer state in the “Great Game” between Russia and Britain.

scienceEducation.value: Adult literacy about 43% (2018); girls are barred from returning to secondary schools under the Taliban.

openness.value: Amanullah Khan’s modernising reforms of the 1920s, such as co-educational schools, provoked a civil war (1928–29).

communicationTransport.value: The Salang Tunnel (1964) through the Hindu Kush; only three short rail links.

religion.value: Almost entirely Muslim: about 90% Sunni and 7% Shia.

artsArchitecture.value: Carpets, Herat miniatures, the destroyed Buddhas of Bamiyan (2001).

socialStructure.value: Pashtun, Tajik, Hazara, Uzbek and other peoples.

dailyLife.value: Mud-brick houses in villages; bread (naan), rice (pulao), tea.

neighbours.value: Iran, Pakistan, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan, Tajikistan, China.

ideasReligions.value: Communist rule from the 1978 Saur Revolution until 1992.

colonisation.value: Became free of foreign political hegemony after the Third Anglo-Afghan War in 1919.

riseSignals.value: The modern state began with the Durrani Empire under Ahmad Shah Durrani (1747).

peakPeriod.value: The Durrani Empire in the 1750s–60s reached India.

outcome.value: Still in existence; the Taliban government is not widely recognised.

overallCertainty.value: Basic facts documented; population and war figures are uncertain.
